newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks seen consolidating on HK handover.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks seen consolidating on HK handover.

text.p: Taiwan share prices were expected to consolidate at current levels on Wednesday with investors likely to adopt a wait-and-see attitude on Hong Kong following its handover, brokers said.
On Monday, the index ended up 5.80 points or 0.06 percent at 9,030.28, a seven-year closing high. The market was closed on Tuesday on because of bank semiannual account settlements.

"So far, Hong Kong's return (to China) seems to be going smoothly, but investors should step to the sidelines for some time to see the handover situation and the Hong Kong stock market's reaction," said Allen Huang of National Securities.
A 8,980-9,080 range was seen for Wednesday.

Huang said the market likely would not react much to news on Tuesday that Taiwan's Securities and Futures Commission was lifting a restriction which prevented companies from listing shares simultaneously in the Taiwan stock exchange and foreign bourses.
The liberalisation, effective from July 2, applies to local Taiwan companies as well as foreign firms.

"It surely is positive news, which will help expand our capital market and help local firms raise funds overseas and vice versa for foreign companies in Taiwan," Huang said. "But the effect should be a long-term one, and I cannot see how big the impact will be," Huang said.
